classes.name: Election of the President
classes.name_en: President, by declared support of the elected members
classes.locator: Constitution of Botswana, s. 32 (each parliamentary candidate declares which presidential candidate they support; the candidate backed by more than half the elected members is President) and s. 35 (the National Assembly elects on a vacancy)
classes.note: No separate ballot: the outcome follows from the National Assembly general election. In 1965 the office was Prime Minister; the presidency dates from independence (30 September 1966).

classes.name: Specially elected Members of the National Assembly
classes.name_en: Specially elected members of the National Assembly
classes.locator: Constitution of Botswana, s. 58 (specially elected members, elected by the National Assembly on the nomination of the President)
classes.disposition_reason: The National Assembly elects them from the President's nominees by its own vote after the general election; there is no public ballot and no published count.

classes.name: Election of the Speaker of the National Assembly
classes.locator: Constitution of Botswana, s. 59 (the Speaker is elected by the members of the National Assembly)
classes.disposition_reason: An internal vote of the National Assembly at its first sitting, recorded in Hansard rather than run or published as an election.

classes.name: Ntlo ya Dikgosi
classes.name_en: House of Chiefs (Ntlo ya Dikgosi), elected members
classes.locator: Constitution of Botswana, ss. 77-79 (composition of Ntlo ya Dikgosi: ex officio dikgosi, members elected in regional electoral colleges, and members appointed by the President)
classes.disposition_reason: Its elected members are chosen by electoral colleges of dikgosi and headmen in each region, not by the public, and no results are published; the house advises Parliament and does not legislate.

classes.name: Referendum
classes.locator: Constitution of Botswana, s. 89(3) (a bill altering an entrenched section goes to a referendum after passing the National Assembly)
classes.note: Called by writ of the President under the Referendum Act. Held in 1987 (Supervisor of Elections), 1997 (three questions: an independent electoral commission, voting from abroad, and a voting age of 18), and 2001 (eight questions on the judiciary). A referendum on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill No. 14 of 2025 (Constitutional Court) is announced with no date set.

dates.note: One question, creating the office of Supervisor of Elections; not yet taken from an official record.

classes.name: Local government (council) elections
classes.name_en: District, city, and town councils, ward councillors
classes.locator: Local Government Act, 2012 (Cap. 40:01): each council's elected councillors, one per ward (polling district)
classes.finest_note: Ward (polling district); each ward elects one councillor by plurality
classes.note: Councils were set up under the District Councils Law, 1965 and the Town Council Regulations, 1966; from 1969 their elections fall on the general election day. The Minister also nominates councillors, who are not elected. 490 wards from the 2002 demarcation through 2019, 609 from 2024.

classes.name: Election of council chairpersons and mayors
classes.locator: Local Government Act, 2012 (Cap. 40:01): each council elects its chairperson (district councils) or mayor (city and town councils) from among its councillors
classes.disposition_reason: Each council elects its chairperson or mayor from among its members at its first meeting; the state does not run or publish these votes.

classes.name: Village Development Committees
classes.locator: Local Government Act, 2012 (Cap. 40:01) and the council by-laws under it
classes.disposition_reason: Committee members are chosen at a village kgotla meeting, not at a poll run by the Independent Electoral Commission, and no results are published.

classes.name: Party primary elections
classes.locator: Electoral Act (Cap. 02:09): candidates are nominated by registered voters at the returning officer; parties select their candidates under their own rules
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their candidates (for example in party primaries) under their own constitutions; the state neither runs nor publishes them.

classes.name: Bechuanaland Protectorate Legislative Council
classes.name_en: Legislative Council of the Bechuanaland Protectorate
classes.locator: Bechuanaland Protectorate (Constitution) Order in Council, 1960 (Legislative Council of official, nominated, and elected members)
classes.disposition_reason: Its elected members were chosen on separate racial rolls and through the African Council before self-government; no official record of the 1961 results is published online, and the protectorate records sit with the Botswana National Archives.
